item.title: Whole-body imaging reveals where drugs bind at single-cell resolution
item.description: When you take a drug, where in your body does it actually go? For most medications, scientists can make only educated guesses about the answer to this question.

item.title: Research highlights a potential therapeutic strategy for vascular dementia
item.description: A possible new treatment for impaired brain blood flow and related dementias is on the horizon.

item.title: A senescence-based therapeutic approach for temporal lobe epilepsy
item.description: Temporal lobe epilepsy, which results in recurring seizures and cognitive dysfunction, is associated with premature aging of brain cells.

item.title: Reframing the role of MCL1 in cancer signaling and metabolism
item.description: A study by the Mildred Scheel Early Career Center group led by Dr. Mohamed Elgendy at the TUD Faculty of Medicine provides fundamental insights into cancer biology.

item.title: Researchers create the most detailed 3D maps of the human genome
item.description: In a landmark effort to understand how the physical structure of our DNA influences human biology, Northwestern investigators and the 4D Nucleome Project have unveiled the most detailed maps to date of the genome's three‑dimensional organization across time and space, according to a new study published in Nature.

item.title: Early brain connectivity predicts recovery after traumatic brain injury
item.description: After traumatic brain injury (TBI), some patients may recover completely, while others retain severe disabilities.

item.title: THC products provide small improvements in pain but carry side effects
item.description: A new systematic evidence review finds that cannabis products that carry relatively high levels of the psychoactive compound tetrahydrocannabinol, commonly known as THC, may provide short-term improvements in pain and function.

item.title: Menopause hormone therapy not linked to dementia risk in women
item.description: A major review of prior research has found no evidence that menopause hormone therapy either increases or decreases dementia risk in post-menopausal women, in a new study led by University College London (UCL) researchers.

item.title: Wearable AI device detects early signs of frailty in older adults
item.description: University of Arizona researchers in the Gutruf Lab have developed a comfortable, easy-to-use wearable device that incorporates artificial intelligence to detect subtle warning signs of frailty, signifying a leap forward in elderly care.

item.title: Spatial computing explains how the brain organizes cognition
item.description: Our thoughts are specified by our knowledge and plans, yet our cognition can also be fast and flexible in handling new information.
